description: A six-cup bellows vacuum gripper (stdlib SuctionCup, VacuumGenerator) moves a 10 kg carton 1 m: pick, lift, transfer, lower, place. Every model is the same plant with other global parameters (separate-generators adds a generator per cup). design/design.py derives the operating vacuum, the holding limits, the pick-up and the shortest safe move per profile, yaw, tilt and porosity; the checks pin the claims of each scenario against those numbers.

checks.note: pick-up: the vacuum build-up 50 ms after the valve opens matches the lumped manifold + six-cup ODE of design/sizing.py (18.06 kPa)
operating vacuum: the 60 l/min ejector curve meets the leak demand (lip roughness + Darcy flow through cardboard, 6 cups) at 48.33 kPa per cup (sizing.operating_vacuum)
the generator delivers the total leak flow of the six cups, 11.6 l/min of free air, at the operating point
the 1.75 s S-curve transfer keeps every cup's utilisation U at or below 1/S = 0.5 (safety factor 2): the shortest such S-curve move found by design.py is 1.69 s
cup 2: the same bound
cup 3: the same bound
cup 4: the same bound
cup 5: the same bound
cup 6: the same bound
the parcel stays on the gripper until the release
no cup loses its seal before the release
the parcel is placed on the place mark, 1 m from the pick position
the parcel survives the acceleration and the cruise of the 0.7 s trapezoid (9.2 m/s^2) ...
... but the acceleration step at the deceleration rings the bellows: the cups peel one after the other and all six lose their seal
the parcel is dropped before the place position
the same 0.7 s transfer as an S-curve (13.1 m/s^2 peak, 43 % more than the trapezoid, but finite jerk) keeps the parcel
no cup loses its seal before the release
the parcel arrives (it slides about 1 cm on the lips during the hard deceleration)
the 1.25 s cycloidal move (4.0 m/s^2) with the gripper tilted along the specific force keeps U <= 0.5; held level the same move reaches U = 0.62 (design.py)
cup 2: the same bound
cup 3: the same bound
cup 4: the same bound
cup 5: the same bound
cup 6: the same bound
the tilt servo turns the gripper up to 15.2 deg (atan(4.0/9.81) = 22 deg commanded, saturated by th_max = 20 deg through tanh)
the parcel stays on the gripper
no cup loses its seal before the release

porous parcel on a 36 l/min generator: the Darcy flow through the material (2e-6 m/(s*Pa)) pulls the operating vacuum down to 21.6 kPa, where the generator curve meets the leak demand (sizing.operating_vacuum)
the generator runs at 64 % of its free flow just to feed the leaks
it survives the lift and the acceleration of the 1.2 s move ...
... and is lost in the deceleration (4.5 m/s^2); with the 60 l/min generator (29 kPa) the same move holds (design.py)
cup 1 over the parcel edge (20 mm^2 extra leak) cannot build vacuum (analytic 1.87 kPa) ...
... and through the common manifold its leak flow pulls every other cup down to 16.7 kPa (analytic operating point)
16.7 kPa cannot lift 10 kg with five cups: all cups are lost at the lift
the parcel stays on the conveyor
the per-cup flow valve of cup 1 closes (bleed 2 %): cup 1 stays at atmosphere ...
... and the five good cups keep 48.7 kPa (slightly more than with six sealed cups: one cup less leaks into the manifold)
five cups carry the parcel to the place position
only cup 1 is lost
one 10 l/min generator per cup: a good cup reaches the same 48.33 kPa as with the shared 60 l/min generator, independent of the leaking cup 1
five cups carry the parcel
only cup 1 is lost
